premises: Microstructural descriptors (phase fractions, interfacial characteristics, misfit strain, length scales) can be quantitatively linked to macroscopic mechanical properties.
Such descriptors can be obtained from pre-characterization of the hierarchical heterostructure in HfNbTiVAl10.
A surrogate model using these static descriptors can capture the essential physics of elasticity, yield, and crack initiation.
The surrogate model can achieve ±5–10% error in predicting Young’s modulus, yield strength, and fracture parameters relative to experiments.
The surrogate model can reduce computation time by roughly an order of magnitude compared to full-scale simulations.
